How we work

From opportunity to shared progress.

AAC actively identifies opportunities, convenes stakeholders and builds the capability and partnerships that help initiatives move forward across Australia and Asia.

01

Discover opportunities

Identify emerging needs, shared priorities and where Australia–Asia collaboration can create value.

IN PRACTICE

Recognising opportunities to connect Australian entrepreneurship expertise with institutions across Asia seeking to develop entrepreneurial capabilities.

02

Build capability

Bring relevant knowledge, experience and expertise together so people and organisations are ready to act.

IN PRACTICE

Helping businesses strengthen market understanding and scaling readiness before pursuing Southeast Asian opportunities.

03

Enable collaboration

Convene complementary stakeholders and help promising relationships progress into practical initiatives.

IN PRACTICE

Bringing organisations together to explore cross-border innovation around longer lives.

Shared priorities · Regional possibilities

Where opportunities take shape.

AIA's four strategic themes provide a lens for discovering opportunities and building collaborations across Australia and Asia.

01 / 04

Agriculture

Food systems, agritech and sustainable production across changing markets.

Opportunity in practice

Connecting Australian agricultural innovation and expertise with regional partners exploring more resilient food systems.

02 / 04

Climate

Climate resilience, sustainable technologies and the transition to lower-impact economies.

Opportunity in practice

Bringing innovators and industry stakeholders together to explore cooling, energy efficiency or climate-adaptation opportunities.

03 / 04

People

Education, entrepreneurship, leadership and the capabilities to navigate change.

Opportunity in practice

Developing Australia–Asia entrepreneurship learning and educator capability initiatives with institutions and practitioners.

04 / 04

Health

Healthy ageing, longer lives and innovations that improve wellbeing and participation.

Opportunity in practice

Convening partners around the Future of Longer Lives, from lifelong learning to technology-enabled independence.

The experience behind AAC

Both sides of the border. First-hand.

Born and raised in Singapore and based in Melbourne for more than a decade, AIA co-founder Li Si Wong brings lived experience of navigating markets, building businesses and working across Australia and Asia.

That perspective shapes AAC's approach: understanding the people, contexts and capabilities that help opportunities take shape.

“Entering new markets is daunting, no matter how seasoned you are. Aus–Asia Connect helped us carve out our core ICP in Australia and find the right positioning — while staying true to our brand. Their suggestions are actionable and grounded in deep reasoning.”
Azmeen AnsarHead of Marketing, Perx
“Aus–Asia Connect provides an insightful bridge between two cultures — Singapore and Australia. With genuine business acumen and experience, they build understanding and identify opportunities for companies from either nation.”
Andrea PlawutskySenior Program Manager, Haymarket HQ

An Australian partnership

Alliance Institute Australia × Wade Institute of Entrepreneurship

Wade Institute of Entrepreneurship · Ormond College, University of Melbourne

Global perspectives. Regional relevance.

Alliance Institute Australia partners with the Wade Institute of Entrepreneurship at Ormond College, University of Melbourne, combining established Australian entrepreneurship education expertise with regional insights to build capability across Asia.

Through AAC, this partnership can help connect regional opportunities with practical learning, entrepreneurial thinking and complementary expertise.

“Our partnership creates exciting possibilities to bring entrepreneurial thinking and practical learning to people and organisations across different stages of life.”Jessica Christiansen-Franks · Managing Director, Wade Institute of Entrepreneurship
